title: Animations in UIKit and SwiftUI
summary: UIKit animates by changing view properties inside `UIView.animate`; SwiftUI animates when state changes inside `withAnimation` or with `.animation(_:value:)`. Both hand the work to Core Animation.
body: **In simple words:** You give the start and end values (position, alpha, size), and the system draws the in-between frames smoothly.

**UIKit:** `UIView.animate(withDuration:) { view.alpha = 0 }` for simple cases; spring animations for natural motion; `UIViewPropertyAnimator` when you need to pause, reverse or drive it with a gesture (interactive). Animate constraint changes by updating constraints and calling `layoutIfNeeded()` inside the block.

**Core Animation:** `CABasicAnimation`/`CAKeyframeAnimation` on layers for things UIView cannot animate (e.g. shape paths, gradients). Note: the layer's model value does not change automatically - set the final value yourself.

**SwiftUI:** `withAnimation(.spring) { isExpanded.toggle() }` animates every view affected by that state change. `.animation(.easeInOut, value: x)` animates when `x` changes. `.transition(.slide)` for views being inserted/removed. `matchedGeometryEffect` for hero animations between views.
**Performance:** animate `transform` and `opacity` (cheap for the GPU) rather than frames that trigger layout; avoid offscreen-rendered effects during animation.
keyPoints: Constraint animations: change constants, then `layoutIfNeeded()` in the animation block.
Prefer transform/opacity animations; respect Reduce Motion.

mistakes: Using the deprecated `.animation(_:)` modifier without a `value`, which animates unexpected changes.
Animating with a `Timer` and setting frames manually every tick.
followups: **How do you make an interactive dismiss animation?** `UIViewPropertyAnimator` driven by a pan gesture's progress, or a custom `UIViewControllerInteractiveTransitioning`.
**Why does my CABasicAnimation jump back at the end?** The layer's model value was not updated to the final value.
